name: greenroom
description: A local, no-code app for running Playwright end-to-end checks against your live web app and reviewing the results.

scripts.deps:refresh: for p in batch grain mill proof pantry; do bun add @tjakoen/$p@github:tjakoen/$p#$(git ls-remote https://github.com/tjakoen/$p.git main | cut -c1-7); done

//dependencies: INTENTIONALLY LOCKLESS (bun.lock gitignored). greenroom -> @tjakoen/pantry(git) -> {batch,grain,mill,proof}(git) is a depth-2+ nested github git-dep graph that bun (1.3.14 + 1.2.21) cannot resolve from scratch: deps:refresh, plain `bun install`, AND `bun install --frozen-lockfile` all fail on pantry's transitive layer specs every run (see the bread-bun-nested-git blocker). Unlike the bread umbrella (bunx-only, truly needs no lock), greenroom is a real app that runs from node_modules — so an EXISTING checkout's node_modules is what serves it; committing a lock only bought a stale/inconsistent one (pkg pantry#b7d75dc vs a lock stuck at #c629008) that can't be regenerated. Removing it resolves that inconsistency. TRADEOFF: a fresh clone can't reinstall from zero until the nesting is flattened or bun is fixed. Do NOT try to regenerate a lock here — retrying never converges. GRAIN PIN NOTE: grain#5b0116c is the target (it adds the b-select + chip-group P3 needs); because the nested-git wall blocks a real reinstall, those two component dirs are VENDORED directly into node_modules/@tjakoen/grain/components (additive — they don't exist at the older resolved tree, so this can't regress the shell). The rest of node_modules/@tjakoen/grain remains the previously-resolved tree; a future clean install (once the nesting is flattened / bun is fixed) fetches 5b0116c and supersedes the vendored copies.
